newsitem.title: JORDAN: Housing Bank lifts Amman bourse volume.
newsitem.headline: Housing Bank lifts Amman bourse volume.

text.p: Shares on the Jordanian stock exchange rose at the end of weekly trade on Wednesday, lifted by some blue-chip interest in heavy turnover boosted by large block trade in Housing Bank, brokers said.
The official 60-share Amman Financial Market (AFM) index rose 0.43 percent to 150.76 points in trade worth 1,851,849 dinars ($2.6 million), the highest daily volume since early January.

The high turnover was mainly attributed to a large trade in Housing Bank, which announced last week it planned to double its capital to 50 million dinars. It closed unchanged at 4.77 dinars after a deal worth 1,568,615 dinars.
Another banking stock, Jordan National Bank, saw some active trade which helped it gain 0.03 dinars to 1.79 dinars in trade worth 39,615 dinars.

Brokers said limited buying on some industrial blue chips including Jordan Electric Power and Arab Pharmaceutical Manufacturing helped buttress the market. They rose 0.06 dinars to 1.67 dinars and 0.08 dinars to 3.56 dinars respectively.
Advancing shares led declining issues by 21 to 8. Shares in another 12 companies were traded but closed unchanged.
But institutional buyers who could help inject purchasing power are still absent in daily activity now mainly executed by small floor traders, brokers said.
A recent wave of selling eased on newly-listed NAMICO, which produces copper wire for telecommunications and electricity firms, helping stabilise prices at the parallel market.
It was unchanged at 0.52 dinars in trade worth 26,869 dinars.
The private Pearl Index of the 45 best-performing shares in terms of turnover and financial performance rose 0.56 percent to 79.28 points, down 4.94 percent since the start of the year.
